chunks: From him, from Imran, from Ayyub, from Safwan, from Ali al-Saqqaf, who said:
I asked him about the dust of the goldsmiths, and that we sell it. He said: 'Can you not make it permissible (halal) from its owner?'
I said: 'No, if I tell him, he will suspect me (of cheating).' He said: 'Sell it.'
I said: 'With what shall we sell it?' He said: 'With food.'
I said: 'Then what shall I do with it?' He said: 'Give it in charity, either for yourself or for his family.'
I said: 'If he is a needy relative, I will connect with him (through kinship ties).' He said: 'Yes.'

key_terms.بِطَعَامٍ: with food (as a medium of exchange)

ai.seo_question: How to sell goldsmiths' dust according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates the Shia juristic principle of *istihsan* (juristic preference) in resolving *gharar* (uncertainty) regarding mixed goods; by converting the uncertain gold dust into a certain commodity like food, the transaction becomes valid. Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) further refines the ethical application by permitting the charity to be directed toward a needy relative, thereby combining commercial validity with the virtue of *silat al-rahim* (maintaining kinship ties).
